newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke-Buba's steady rate policy well advised.
newsitem.headline: Welteke-Buba's steady rate policy well advised.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Tuesday that the Bundesbank was well advised to maintain its current steady policy on key interest rates.
Welteke, who is also head of the central bank of the state of Hesse, said the Bundesbank had made any necessary changes in interest rate policy the last time it cut rates.

"At the moment the Bundesbank is well advised to follow a straight course on interest rates and thereby stabilise the expectations of the financial markets," Welteke said at the fringes of a meeting of Germany's IG Metall trade union.
Welteke said that the Bundesbank would not welcome a further rise in the dollar.
He said that the appreciation of the dollar in recent months had led to a slight rise in import prices, which could have a delayed impact on producer and later on consumer prices.
"Because of this we cannot welcome a further rise in the dollar," said Welteke.
The dollar fell by around a pfennig after Welteke's comments. The dollar stood at around 1.7227/32 against the mark at 1338 GMT.
